---
title: "suest2"
subtitle: "Seemingly unrelated estimation for most models in Stata, with margins support"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

`suest2` combines models that were estimated separately into one set of
results, including cross-model covariances which are necessary for tests
across models. After `suest2`, coefficients, predictions, and marginal effects
from different models can be tested against each other with
[`mecompare`](../mecompare/index.html) or with `test`, `lincom`,
`nlcom`, or `margins`. [`mecompare`](../mecompare/index.html) is written
specifically to automate a range of cross-model comparisons of effects.

`suest2` extends Stata's `suest` to panel, multilevel, weighted, survey,
multiply-imputed, generalized ordered, and instrumental-variable models, and
it lets `predict` and `margins` select a constituent model from the combined
system, so that most any post-estimation work -- predictions, marginal
effects, graphs of either -- can be done within and across models.

`suest2` is used by [`mecompare`](../mecompare/index.html), [`meinequality`](../meinequality/index.html),
and [`totalme`](../totalme/index.html) to combine model estimates before
those commands' post-estimation calculations, and those three packages require
it.

## Installation

```stata
net install suest2, from("https://tdmize.github.io/data") replace
```


## Where to start

- [Usage](usage.html): the workflow, the options of `suest2`, how to point

  data, and multiple imputation.
- [Predictions and graphs](plotting.html): `margins`, `marginsplot`, and

  across models with its confidence interval, and predicted probabilities
  from binary, ordinal, and multinomial models.
- [Examples from the help file](help-examples.html): single-level, panel,
  multilevel, and instrumental-variable systems, run in full.
- The [help file](help.html), rendered from the installed version
  (`help suest2` in Stata).

## Basic use

Fit and store the models, then combine them:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
sysuse nlsw88, clear
drop if missing(union)

quietly logit union i.collgrad c.age i.south, vce(robust)
estimates store m1

quietly logit union i.collgrad c.age i.south c.wage c.ttl_exp, vce(robust)
estimates store m2

suest2 m1 m2
<</dd_do>>
```

The combined results are now the active estimates. Each model is an equation,
named after the stored estimate, so `lincom`, `test`, and `nlcom` can compare
coefficients across the models:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
lincom [m1_union]1.collgrad - [m2_union]1.collgrad
<</dd_do>>
```

And [`mecompare`](../mecompare/index.html) with no `models()` option picks up
the two models of the system:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare i.collgrad age
<</dd_do>>
```
